knownGaps.summary: node-security/no-unbounded-decompression is silent on zlib.createGunzip(), zlib.createUnzip() and unzipper.Extract(); this generic CWE-770 rule reports all three
knownGaps.why: Not a double-report — exactly one finding per shape — but the dedicated CWE-409 rule does not see its own canonical sink, and all 3 of this rule's surviving real-source findings live in that overlap. Fixing it means deciding which rule owns decompression, which is a taxonomy decision across two plugins
knownGaps.reopenWhen: the CWE-409/CWE-770 ownership boundary is settled

knownGaps.summary: A decompression whose output bytes are counted against a threshold in the same function is treated as bounded, even when that threshold is opt-in and defaults to unlimited
knownGaps.why: axios counts decompressed bytes against maxContentLength, whose default is -1. The rule stops reporting the library that implements the mechanism; it cannot see whether a consumer enabled it. Reporting anyway would mean reporting the fix the author already applied
knownGaps.reopenWhen: the rule can see a config default, or the check moves to the call site that sets maxContentLength

knownGaps.summary: Buffer.alloc(n) where n is a function parameter with no visible initializer is not reported
knownGaps.why: Deliberate. Taint starts at a binding this file can see the value of; assuming a parameter named `data` or `size` is attacker-controlled is what produced the 173 findings this rule was fixed for
knownGaps.reopenWhen: cross-file taint is available, which no rule in this ecosystem has today

knownGaps.summary: No XML entity-expansion detection. The path was removed 2026-08-18 after xml2js was measured unable to expand entities at all
knownGaps.why: The removed check could only ever fire on xml2js, which parses through sax-js and rejects custom entity references outright. libxmljs `noent: true` IS a real sink and is a different API on a different module
knownGaps.reopenWhen: a rule is written against a parser whose entity handling was actually measured
